## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kukkuḷakathā* ("Discussion on Burning Embers") is the eighth debate of the second chapter (*vagga*) of the *Kathāvatthu* in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Bareau 1955; Warder 2000]. According to the commentary by Buddhaghosa, the controversy is directed against the Gokulikas (also designated in various traditions as Kaukkuṭikas or Kukkuḷikas) [Bareau 1955; Williams 2000; Warder 2000]. This school held the view that all conditioned formations (*saṅkhārā*) without exception (*anodhiṁ katvā*) are nothing but a mass of burning embers or glowing cinders (*kukkuḷa*) [Bareau 1955; Williams 2000]. The Gokulikas supported this position by appealing to canonical discourse statements wherein the Buddha declared that all conditioned phenomena are ablaze (*āditta*) with the fires of greed, hatred, and delusion [Bareau 1955; Warder 2000]. The *Kathāvatthu* criticizes this doctrine as an illegitimate over-generalization that errs by denying the reality of any worldly happiness or pleasure whatsoever, portraying phenomenal existence as unrelieved suffering [Williams 2000; Warder 2000].

SuttaCentral identifies a passage-level parallel to this debate in the Jaina text *Isibhāsiyāiṁ* 38.1, and notes shared textual references with canonical discourses including the *Cūḷasaccaka Sutta* (MN 35), the *Ādittasutta* (SN 22.61; SN 35.28), the *Khaṇasutta* (SN 35.135), the *Bhikkhusutta* (SN 36.20), the Vinaya *Mahākhandhaka* (Kd 1), and Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* parallels (SĀ 197, SĀ 210) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus reports extensive Pali-internal text reuse across 895 matching passages in 89 texts, most heavily with the *Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta* (SN 35, notably §5.5–5.12 matching SN 35.135), the Vinaya *Mahākhandhaka* (Kd 1), other *Kathāvatthu* debates (such as Kv 1.1 and Kv 7.4), the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37), and the *Vedanā Saṁyutta* (SN 36) [DharmaNexus]. Both SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus agree on alignments with the Vinaya *Mahākhandhaka* / *Saṅghabhedavastu* and the *Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta* / *Saṁyuktāgama* (T 99) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records machine alignments with Sanskrit texts including the *Saṅghabhedavastu* and *Arthaviniścayasūtra*, as well as Tibetan translations of Mahāyāna sūtras such as the *Pitāputrasamāgamana* (D 60) and *Lalitavistara* (D 95) [DharmaNexus].
